internals.title: Implementation details
internals.subtitle: How energy is classified into tariff slots, running totals are persisted, and daily kWh are registered in Home Assistant statistics — while your physical meters remain the source of truth.
internals.s_overview_p1: At a high level: the coordinator watches configured energy entities (total_increasing kWh). Each positive delta is tagged with the tariff slot active when the delta occurred, then summed into per-source totals and per-day / per-slot buckets. Calendar days and midnight maintenance follow your Home Assistant default time zone (Settings → System → General). When a calendar day in that timezone is complete, those buckets feed Home Assistant external statistics for durable per-slot and per-source graphs. A JSON Store holds running sums and recent day maps so restarts stay consistent. EDF Tempo slot rules (HP/HC windows and supply-day boundaries) still use France civil time so they stay aligned with official calendars.
internals.s_overview_p2_html: Recorder history for the entities you selected remains the external SSOT for raw meter values; integration SSOT sensors expose the internally accumulated totals used for slot splits and cost snapshots.
internals.s_lovelace_p1: The integration registers a dashboard resource pointing at /hub_energie/hub-energie-card-boot.js. That boot file is a small loader; it pulls in the full card module. The compiled bundle ships inside custom_components/hub_energie/frontend/dist/ and is served from your instance under /hub_energie/.
internals.s_lovelace_p2_html: On startup and when you reload the integration, the resource entry is refreshed with a cache-busting ?v=… query string (same mechanism as Settings → Dashboards → Resources) so browsers load new JavaScript. Storage-mode dashboards pick this up automatically; if your dashboards are YAML-only, you must add the resource yourself (see the expandable steps under Documentation → Lovelace card).
internals.s_sources_p1: Each configured meter maps to a source key (for example grid import, grid export, solar, per-battery charge and discharge). The expected key set comes from your configuration: only sources bound to an entity participate in statistics writes. Three-phase setups can use summed “virtual” entities for bookkeeping while still reading phase meters upstream.
internals.s_sources_p2: Long-term statistics writes require a complete source matrix for a finished day; if any expected source is missing from the internal day map, that day is skipped — avoiding silent partial writes.
internals.s_slots_p1_html: EDF Tempo defines six price bands encoded as slot ids: bleu_hc, bleu_hp, blanc_hc, blanc_hp, rouge_hc, rouge_hp. BASE maps to HP only; HP/HC uses two bands under the same naming scheme; non-EDF manual tariffs keep HC/HP ids for compatibility while prices come from your tables.
internals.s_slots_p2_html: An additional attribution bucket unknown exists only in live bookkeeping when no definite slot can be resolved. Completed days written to Recorder statistics use the six canonical slots; the unknown bucket appears in diagnostics for transparency.
internals.s_attr_h: How a delta picks a slot
internals.s_attr_p1: When a delta is applied, the coordinator resolves the current slot in this order: primary resolver (Tempo calendar or colour, optional user slot sensor, wall-clock off-peak rules), then a stable “last known good” slot if the primary result is ambiguous, then a schedule-only fallback from frozen EDF runtime fields and the instance default time zone. If nothing maps to a canonical slot, attribution is unknown — energy is still accumulated so nothing is dropped silently.
internals.s_attr_p2_html: The resolution method is recorded alongside the delta (direct, fallback_last_known, fallback_schedule, unknown) so diagnostics can explain why a given bucket grew.
internals.s_reinjection_p1: When the hub sees positive grid export power together with PV and optional battery charge, it labels a diagnostic “cause” for transparency (not for billing). The decision tree is deterministic: thresholds come from Configure → Advanced: reinjection tuning and map directly to fields in code (see classify_reinjection_cause in the integration).
internals.s_reinjection_formula_html: Dynamic export bar used in several branches: export_vs_solar = max(min_export_w, fraction × solar_w). Export must meet or exceed this bar (and solar must be at least the “min solar for classification” watts) before solar-led explanations are considered.
internals.s_reinjection_cat_html:
• unattributed — export at or below the ignore threshold (noise / no meaningful export); or a late fallback when solar is too low to apply solar-heavy rules.
  • switch_latency — export has lasted at most the configured seconds and power stays under the latency ceiling (typical short inverter or measurement bump).
  • battery_full_or_absent — no battery configured; or SOC/limits suggest the pack cannot absorb surplus while export is high versus PV; or SOC is at/above the configured “full” fraction with little charge power.
  • solar_surplus — strong PV versus export threshold while the battery is not charging significantly; or PV is high enough with export above the dynamic bar while the pack is still filling from solar; or explicit “battery charging while exporting” branch when charge power is above the significance watts.
internals.s_reinjection_link_setup_help_: Field-by-field wording in Home Assistant matches the reinjection step help and delta caps step help tables (generated from the same strings).
internals.s_delta_p1: Only positive deltas count toward consumption totals. Small negative steps can be treated as meter jitter (re-baselining without consuming energy); larger negative changes may trigger re-anchoring or discards per integration thresholds. Caps limit runaway spikes from bad data.
internals.s_delta_p2: Drift between the external meter reading and the internal running sum is tracked per source so the health model can surface inconsistent or degraded trust without silently skewing costs.
internals.s_day_p1: Per-day buckets and the ISO day written to statistics follow your Home Assistant default time zone. During scheduled midnight maintenance (local midnight) the integration finalizes yesterday’s buckets, persists them, writes Recorder statistics for that ISO day, prunes obsolete accumulator rows, and refreshes the public snapshot. EDF Tempo calendars and official HP/HC windows remain defined in France civil time.
internals.s_day_p2: If Home Assistant was offline across a boundary, catch-up writes can run after restart: the Store records which days were exported successfully to avoid duplicate statistics inserts when possible.
internals.s_store_p1_html: The integration persists totals per source, a map of slot_day_kwh[day][source][slot], last raw meter readings, drift anchors, which statistic days were written, optional grid-export / battery-split diagnostics, and the last known cumulative floors used for long-term statistics metadata. Debounced saves reduce disk churn on busy systems.
internals.s_store_p2: If the Store payload is corrupt or no longer trustworthy, a guarded path can rebuild internal totals from Recorder history for completed days before normal operation resumes — exposing a rebuilding trust state in the meantime.
internals.s_lts_p1_html: For each finished day and each (source, slot) pair among the six canonical Tempo slots, the integration calls Home Assistant’s external statistics API with a TOTAL_INCREASING sum. Statistic ids look like hub_energie:slot_<source>_<slot>_kwh with the source segment normalized for id safety. The daily increment is added to the previous cumulative sum kept with the Store so the Recorder sees one continuous monotonic series per statistic.
internals.s_lts_p2: These series are the preferred basis for historical analytics that need stable per-slot kWh — lighter than parsing raw template attributes, and aligned with how the Energy dashboard consumes statistics.
internals.s_rebuild_p1: When feasible, the integration replays prior external statistic samples to recover daily slot totals and rebuild the cumulative floor map — then reconciles against current entity readings. Long-term statistic series live in the Recorder database while detailed per-slot day matrices live in the Store; both must stay aligned after restores or migrations.
internals.s_rebuild_p2_html: If the Recorder is temporarily unavailable the rebuild step is skipped with a warning; operation continues, but consult docs/troubleshooting.md if trust / health sensors report issues after major database operations.
internals.s_tel_p1: Per-source delta telemetry includes timestamps, applied kWh, attributed slot, resolution method, gaps between applies, and drift versus the external meter. Aggregated discard counters and last-rejection payloads help trace policy decisions during support. Separate input status flags missing or unavailable entities before energy math runs.
internals.s_tel_p2_html: The health / trust sensor rolls these signals into coarse states such as ok, degraded, rebuilding, or inconsistent with human-readable causes — the same signals the Lovelace card can show in diagnostics.
internals.footer_html: For user-facing setup, return to the integration showcase, visit home-assistant.io, or open the GitLab repository.
ssot.title: Data sources (SSOT)
ssot.intro: Knowing which data is authoritative helps you configure the Energy dashboard correctly and read the right attributes.
ssot.s1_html: The energy entities you select (grid_import_energy, solar, export, per-battery in/out). Recorder history is the source of truth for total kWh from hardware or upstream integrations.
ssot.s2_html: The coordinator accumulates positive deltas into totals and per-day slot kWh. Integration total_increasing SSOT sensors reflect this internal sum, not a full re-read of the meter every cycle.
ssot.s3_html: After each completed calendar day in your Home Assistant default time zone, external statistics hub_energie:slot_<source>_<slot>_kwh are written. Use these (or physical meters) for historical analytics — not raw cost_detail attribute history alone.
